name: NYC Restaurant Pest Citations
pitch: Every NYC restaurant the Health Department cited for rats, mice, roaches or flies in the last 30 days, for small commercial pest control firms; the citation means a reinspection is coming and the owner needs a vendor now.

provenAbroad.what: RatRadar sells restaurant pest citation leads to pest control firms in Boston, Chicago, NYC and San Francisco at $299 a month a metro
Our own Chicago Restaurant Inspection Leads (same signal, live at $39 a month on the Chicago portal)

buyer.who: small structural and rodent pest control businesses in New York City
buyer.reach: NYS DEC public roster of registered pesticide businesses (business name, city, category 7a Structural and Rodent) gives the firm; email through the firm's own website contact page

price.reason: NYC is about 8 times Chicago's monthly pest volume (926 places in Sept vs about 117 a week of all fail kinds in Chicago), so $10 over Chicago's $39 and far under RatRadar's $299 territory plan

competitors.name: RatRadar Territory Leads (one metro, monthly refresh)
Apify Restaurant Inspection Leads (NYC included, $10 per 1,000 rows, pay per result, no monthly plan)

aiQueries.q: A pest control sales guide says health inspection violations create immediate urgency for restaurant prospects (undated page, read today)

data.publisher: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (NYC Open Data)
data.dataset: DOHMH New York City Restaurant Inspection Results (43nn-pn8j)
data.subject: a restaurant cited by the NYC Health Department for live pest evidence (04K rats, 04L mice, 04M roaches, 04N flies) in its most recent inspection; 08A harborage alone is left out
data.countNote: Distinct restaurants (camis) with a pest code 04K rats, 04L mice, 04M roaches, 04N flies or 08A not vermin proof: Jul 809, Aug 918, Sep 926, Oct 1 to 22 544. Metadata: Update Frequency Daily, automated, rows updated 2026-10-22.

license.note: NYC Open Data terms: datasets are offered for information, the City gives no warranty and is not liable for errors, and users accept the NYC.gov terms plus any extra agency terms; nothing bars commercial reuse. The Open Data Law (Local Law 11 of 2012, Admin Code 23-502(d), https://intro.nyc/local-laws/2012-11) says public datasets are offered with no registration, no license and no limits on use; the agency may ask for credit. No indemnity clause found (unlike Chicago).

overlap: launches/chicago-restaurant-inspection-leads.md: same product in a second city; Todd paused that product's outreach until the licenses product is live (decision 4, Oct 22). Hood cleaning is left out: ventilation code 10D hit only 50 NYC places in Sept, too thin.
